title: What is a Network?
description: How devices connect and share things
tagline: How devices connect and share things

sections.title: The Simple Idea
sections.body: A network is just two or more devices connected so they can share things with each other — files, a printer, or the internet. Think of it like a WhatsApp group: everyone is connected, and anyone can send a message to anyone else.
points: Each device on a network is called a host or end device.
Every host needs a unique address (like your home address) so data knows exactly where to go.
Connections can be wires (cables) or wireless (Wi-Fi).

sections.title: Client and Server
sections.body: When you open a website, your computer (the client) asks for a page, and a big computer somewhere (the server) sends it back. One asks, one answers — that is the client/server model.
sections.code:
You (client):     "Give me google.com"
Server:           "Here is the page" ✔

sections.title: From Tiny to Giant
sections.body: Two laptops at home = a small network. A company connects hundreds of devices across buildings. Connect all the networks of the world together and you get the Internet — literally "a network of networks".

sections.title: Why Networks Matter
sections.body: Networks exist because sharing beats copying:

head: Benefit
Real example
rows: Send a document to a coworker instantly
One connection serves the whole house
Backups kept on a server, not lost PCs

sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: know the words host, end device, client, server and "network of networks" — CCNA loves basic definitions.
